title: Sintel
abstract: Colin Levy’s Sintel compresses an epic search into a story of misrecognition. This essay argues that the film creates tragic irony through asymmetric temporal knowledge: the quest’s editing and character alignment keep viewers attached to a remembered relationship while physical evidence signals change. The reading examines the wing scar, movement through environments, the shaman, color and musical narration, together with the open-source production context. This editorial draft has a verified reference ledger but awaits genuine local film frames before publication.
